issues.description:
Element: Animal.messageOnFeed()
Problem statement / UML (problem_statement.md) declares the abstract method as public (+ messageOnFeed():String). The solution implementation (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java) declares the method as protected (protected abstract String messageOnFeed()). This is a visibility mismatch: students reading the UML will expect a public abstract API, while the provided solution uses protected visibility. This can confuse students about the expected API and whether implementing classes should use public or protected, and may cause tests or examples that assume a public method to appear inconsistent.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the visibility consistent with the UML and problem description. Preferably change the abstract method in Animal.java to public: 'public abstract String messageOnFeed();' so it matches the '+' in the UML and the verbal instruction. Alternatively, if protected visibility is intentional, update the problem statement/UML to indicate the method is protected and explain this choice in the task description.
